title: Ops Accelerant: QuickOps surface for runbooks-as-tasks and safe admin utilities
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Build a "QuickOps" surface in the Console and opsctl that exposes curated admin utilities implemented as idempotent, auditable tasks (runbooks-as-tasks). Goals: reduce time-to-resolution for common incidents, lower blast radius for manual admin work, and enable non-expert support engineers to execute safe, pre-approved operations.
acceptance_criteria: Console QuickOps panel lists at least 10 validated runbooks with RBAC/approval gating
Each runbook executes through the task runner with deterministic logs, audit entry written to KMS-backed audit store, and is idempotent in presence of retries
opsctl CLI can execute same runbooks non-interactively for automation and scheduled maintenance
Telemetry: per-step timings, success/failure counts, and per-run cost estimates appear in Console dashboards
Feature-flag gating and canary rollout to 10% of instances, with rollout toggle in infra/flags
technical_notes: Runbook format: YAML task graph (steps with idempotency tokens, retry policies, input validation schema)
Executor: extend existing operator-task-runner to support concurrency limits and step-level 'dry-run' semantics
Secrets: step parameters reference KMS/HSM-stored secrets by name; values never appear in logs
Audit: every run produces a W3C trace-id and an immutable audit blob stored in 'audit-service' S3 bucket with S3 Object Lock (retention configurable by org)
Safety: implement 'safe-mode' for high-risk steps -> requires 2-person approval via SSO and request-scoped MFA token
Telemetry: emit metrics to datadog with tags (runbook, step, team, customer_tier) and traces to Jaeger for latency breakdowns
decisions: Use YAML for runbook authoring to make it accessible to PMs and SREs; validate with JSON Schema during PRs
Leverage existing operator task runner binary rather than a new service to reduce deployment surface and reuse existing telemetry
Approval model: implement 'pre-approval' and 'ad-hoc approval' flows; pre-approved runbooks can be executed by level-1 support, ad-hoc require on-call signoff
Do not persist plain-text secrets in runbook manifests; reference secret ids only
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: Spike complete; prototype YAML spec and local executor implemented (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/392)
2026-02-18: Design review with Console team; wireframes for QuickOps panel accepted with minor UX changes (concurrency selector moved to advanced settings)
2026-02-28: Integration with audit-service schema finalized; compliance sign-off checklist drafted
2026-03-04: Security review kickoff; threat model updated to include replay and privilege escalation scenarios
2026-03-10: Began canary rollout to dev account; first runbook executions logged and metrics flowing to Datadog
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Patel): prefer showing estimated cost per run to help product decisions — added to telemetry goals
Security (Marco Gutierrez): require proof-of-possession for ad-hoc approvals (MFA) and detection for unexpected step parameters — implementing step-level validators
Design (Riley Thompson): recommended adding contextual help and 'why this is safe' microcopy on each QuickOps entry to increase trust from L1 support
SRE (Omar Haddad): asked for a kill-switch in the task runner and a per-org concurrency cap — added to technical notes
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dev accounts (canary) -> Phase 2: internal SRE/Support teams -> Phase 3: 10% org rollout via feature flag -> Phase 4: global rollout. Each phase gated by success criteria in testing_plan and metrics thresholds (failure rate < 0.5%, mean step latency within 2x baseline).
testing_plan: Unit tests for YAML schema + runner; e2e harness that replays recorded runbooks against a sandbox infra; soak test for 48h with synthetic failures; manual runbook dry-runs and MFA approval flows validated in staging; chaos test for network partitions to ensure idempotency
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: quickops.run.failure_rate > 0.5% triggers P1 alert to oncall
Trace-based alert: step latency p95 > 5s for critical steps
Audit ingestion lag > 2 minutes -> paged to compliance oncall
rollback_plan: Disable feature-flag immediately, revoke running executions (task-runner kill-switch) and run compensating runbooks for partial-state steps; notify affected stakeholders via incident channel
notes_for_oncall: If a runbook causes unexpected state, collect run id, trace id, and the audit blob URL; escalate to runbook authoring team (eng-runbooks) and follow compensating steps in runbook metadata
